title: Cell Line Block and Microarray Preparation
author: Rona Ortenberg
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.6pnhdme
materials: Re-suspend cells with the smallest possible volume of cold PBS and transfer them into one well in a 96-wells U-shaped plate (Cellstar, Sigma-Aldrich).

steps.title: Maintain cells to confluence
steps.instruction: Keep cell lines in appropriate medium at 37 °C in a humidified atmosphere of 5 % CO₂; when confluence reaches 70–80 % proceed.

steps.title: Harvest adherent or suspension cells
steps.instruction: For adherent cultures, detach with trypsin solution or cell dissociation solution (do not use a scraper). For suspension cultures, collect cells using gentle pipetting.

steps.title: Count cells and set target number
steps.instruction: Determine cell count; aim for 10–30 × 10⁶ melanoma cells or 100–150 × 10⁶ lymphocytes per block, adjusting for cell size.

steps.title: First centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge cells 5 min at 500 × g, 4 °C.

steps.title: Wash with cold PBS
steps.instruction: Discard supernatant, resuspend pellet in 15 mL cold PBS, then centrifuge 5 min at 515 × g, 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare fixation solution
steps.instruction: In a chemical hood, mix 25 mL 4 % PFA, 24 mL 100 % ethanol, and 1 mL distilled water; mix well.

steps.title: Fix cells
steps.instruction: Resuspend pellet in 15 mL fixation solution, incubate 5 min at room temperature in the hood, then centrifuge 5 min at 1250 × g, 4 °C and discard supernatant.

steps.title: Transfer cells to plate wells
steps.instruction: Aliquot cells into wells of a plate (≈280 µL per well). If additional PBS is needed, centrifuge the plate 5 min at 515 × g, 4 °C and discard supernatant to free space.

substeps.instruction: If extra PBS is required, centrifuge plate 5 min at 515 × g, 4 °C and discard supernatant.

steps.title: Final well centrifugation
steps.instruction: After all cells are in wells, centrifuge plate 5 min at 515 × g, 4 °C and discard supernatant.

steps.title: Embed cells in agarose
steps.instruction: Mix each cell pellet with 100–200 µL melted 0.5 % agarose gel; draw the required agar volume directly from the warmed bath.

steps.title: Place agar‑cell mixture in cassette
steps.instruction: Transfer the agar‑cell pellet to the appropriate tissue‑embedding cassette designated for cell blocks.

steps.title: Paraffin embed block
steps.instruction: Embed the cassette in paraffin using standard surgical‑biopsy conditions (≈48 h), typically performed by a pathology service.

steps.title: Section block for staining
steps.instruction: Cut two 4 µm sections: one for routine H&E staining and one for the specific downstream stain.

steps.title: Stain H&E slide
steps.instruction: Perform H&E staining and verify that cells are homogeneously spread in the block.

steps.title: Prepare tissue microarray
steps.instruction: Using a Tissue Microarrayer (Beecher Instruments) with a 2‑mm gauge needle, drill three 2‑mm cores from each donor cell block into the recipient cell‑line microarray (CMA) block.

steps.title: Incorporate cores by heating
steps.instruction: Heat the completed CMA to 37 °C in the designated oven to fuse the cores into the wax.

steps.title: Verify core placement
steps.instruction: Stain every 40th CMA section with H&E to confirm that all cores are correctly positioned.

steps.title: Cool agarose‑cell plate
steps.instruction: Place the flat‑bottom 96‑well plate at 4 °C for 45 min to solidify the agarose.

steps.title: Extract solid agarose‑cell plugs
steps.instruction: Using a sterile #15 straight‑tip scalpel, gently insert between the solid agarose‑cell structure and the well wall, apply a very gentle sideways force to pop the plug out; ensure the agar was mixed thoroughly to avoid cell loss.

steps.title: Final fixation of plugs
steps.instruction: Place the extracted solid cells‑agarose structures in a cassette; they may remain in a tank of 4 % formaldehyde for several hours before final work‑up.
